control_testing.requirement_basis: Senior management and the accountable AI governance body establish and maintain AI-risk accountability, approve the AI risk framework and appetite, and retain material AI-risk decision rights.

design: 1) Inspect the Board mandate/risk governance charter, AI risk framework and approval records. 2) Confirm the documents assign Board/senior-management accountability, define risk appetite/tolerance oversight, and specify decisions reserved for escalation/approval. 3) Confirm reporting cadence, materiality thresholds and evidence-retention responsibilities are defined. PASS when accountability, decision rights and reporting are formally approved and current; FAIL when any material accountability or approval boundary is missing/ambiguous; NOT TESTABLE when the authoritative governance artefacts cannot be obtained.
operating: 1) Obtain the latest 12 months of AI risk reporting and Board/AI Risk Committee minutes, plus a risk-based sample of material AI approvals or risk acceptances. 2) Trace material issues, breaches and high-risk use cases to an accountable senior-management/Board decision. 3) Verify decisions, actions and overdue items were recorded and followed up. PASS when the approved governance model operated on schedule and material matters were escalated/decided; FAIL when required oversight, decisions or follow-up did not occur; NOT TESTABLE when records are unavailable.

control_testing.objective: Consistent identification of where AI is used

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: The organisation consistently identifies AI use cases and routes them into the applicable governance process before deployment or material change.

design: 1) Inspect the AI intake/identification procedure. 2) Confirm it defines what constitutes an AI use case, scope/exclusions, entry triggers, required intake fields, ownership and the point at which a use case must enter governance. 3) Confirm the process prevents unregistered AI from bypassing triage. PASS when identification criteria, triggers and routing are explicit and controlled; FAIL when material AI use can enter production without identification; NOT TESTABLE when the procedure cannot be evidenced.
operating: 1) Reconcile a sample of new projects, model procurements, production deployments and material changes to the AI inventory/intake records. 2) Identify unmatched items and trace whether they were intentionally out of scope or missed. 3) Verify required intake fields and triage occurred before the relevant lifecycle gate. PASS when sampled AI activity is consistently identified and routed; FAIL when material AI use is missing or entered governance too late; NOT TESTABLE when source populations cannot be reconciled.

play_steps.action: Submit AI use-case intake form: purpose, data used, users, decisions affected, expected benefits.
Register the use-case in the central AI inventory with dependencies and ownership.
Run initial risk-materiality triage scoring impact x complexity x reliance.
Route by materiality: low -> streamlined path; high -> full impact assessment + committee review.

PASS when the inventory population is accurate and reconciles to operational reality; FAIL when duplicate, stale or materially missing records exist without disposition; NOT TESTABLE when the operational population is unavailable.

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: A central AI inventory records the AI systems or models in scope, their versions, use cases, owners, dependencies, risk tier and lifecycle/deployment state, and is maintained under controlled update rules.

design: 1) Inspect the central AI inventory schema and procedure. 2) Confirm required fields include, as applicable, system/model and version, use case, owner, dependencies, data, risk tier, lifecycle state, deployment environment and key control links. 3) Confirm change/update rules, ownership and stale-record handling are defined. PASS when the inventory is central, complete-by-design, attributable and maintained under controlled rules; FAIL when required fields or update controls are missing; NOT TESTABLE when no controlled inventory exists.
operating: 1) Reconcile the inventory to a sample of active production systems, development projects and recent deployments/changes. 2) Test uniqueness, completeness, current lifecycle state and version/use-case linkage. 3) Inspect stale records and confirm remediation/escalation. PASS when the inventory population is accurate and reconciles to operational reality; FAIL when duplicate, stale or materially missing records exist without disposition; NOT TESTABLE when the operational population is unavailable.

design: 1) Inspect the lifecycle risk-assessment procedure and risk-register template. 2) Confirm required stages span design/development, validation, deployment and post-deployment/decommissioning as applicable, with risk owners, controls, inherent/residual risk, due dates and escalation. 3) Confirm linkage to materiality, change and monitoring triggers. PASS when lifecycle coverage, ownership and update triggers are explicit; FAIL when material lifecycle stages or risk treatment are absent; NOT TESTABLE when the controlled lifecycle risk process is unavailable.
operating: 1) Select a sample of AI systems at different lifecycle stages and trace their risk register from initiation through current state. 2) Verify identified risks, mitigations, residual risk, owners, overdue items and changes are updated at lifecycle gates/material events. 3) Confirm material unresolved risks are escalated or formally accepted. PASS when risk identification/assessment operates throughout the sampled lifecycle; FAIL when registers are stale, incomplete or not linked to lifecycle events; NOT TESTABLE when system-level risk records cannot be obtained.

play_steps.action: Identify affected individuals/groups and analyse impact (fairness). Trigger the FEAT assessment per the FEAT Assessment Methodology (Veritas): Ethics & Accountability (F2/F3) set at org level, Fairness (F1) and Transparency (F4) run concurrently for the use case. For high-materiality use cases, initiate independent validation.
Complete privacy impact assessment (DPIA) where personal data is involved.
Document foreseeable misuse, predictable failure modes and proposed mitigations.
Assess societal/environmental impact for material or public-facing systems.
Review and sign off the impact assessment; record residual risk.

control_testing.objective: Pre-deployment review & approval (release criteria)

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: Production release of an AI system is gated by objective criteria, evidence review, authorised approval and applicable independent-validation prerequisites before production action.

design: 1) Inspect the release-gate policy/checklist. 2) Confirm mandatory pre-deployment criteria include applicable validation results, risk assessment, human-oversight readiness, security, monitoring, rollback and required approvals, with clear blocking conditions. 3) Confirm no-deploy/bypass rules and emergency-release handling are defined. PASS when release criteria are explicit, version-specific and approval-controlled; FAIL when production deployment can occur without satisfying mandatory gates; NOT TESTABLE when no controlled release-gate artefact exists.
operating: 1) Select a sample of recent production releases and trace each from final tested/versioned artefact through release checklist, approval and deployment timestamp. 2) Verify mandatory criteria were met before deployment and any exceptions were approved by the required authority. 3) Inspect emergency releases for retrospective testing/approval. PASS when sampled releases demonstrate gate compliance and authorised exceptions; FAIL when bypasses or approvals-after-deployment occur without governed emergency treatment; NOT TESTABLE when release/deployment evidence cannot be reconciled.

play_steps.action: Confirm release criteria are met and deployment environment is ready, including FEAT sign-off (F1-F4) and — for high-materiality models — independent validation sign-off per the FEAT Assessment Methodology §D. No high-materiality model is released without it.
Confirm human-oversight design and rollback / kill-switch plan are in place.
Accountable owner accepts residual risk; committee approves for high-materiality.

control_testing.requirement_basis: AI systems are evaluated and independently validated against defined criteria before deployment, with results, limitations, residual risk and re-validation triggers documented.

design: 1) Inspect the evaluation/testing standard, acceptance criteria and independent-validation procedure. 2) Confirm testing covers relevant performance, robustness, fairness, security, explainability and failure-mode dimensions, with risk-based thresholds and evidence-retention requirements. 3) Confirm independent validation is required where materiality warrants it and that unresolved defects block or condition release. PASS when the evaluation and validation design is risk-based, measurable and independent where required; FAIL when material tests/thresholds or independence are absent; NOT TESTABLE when no controlled test methodology exists.
operating: 1) Select a risk-based sample of validation packages, including at least one high-materiality system where available. 2) Reconcile test scope to approved requirements, review results against thresholds, inspect defects/exceptions and confirm independent validation sign-off. 3) Verify failed/conditional tests resulted in remediation, restricted release or documented approval under policy. PASS when tests were executed as designed and release decisions reflect results; FAIL when material tests were skipped, thresholds ignored or independence bypassed; NOT TESTABLE when validation evidence is incomplete.

Document model & feature selection, design decisions and requirements traceability.
Run testing & evaluation: performance, robustness, fairness/bias, security, explainability.
Independently validate the model (independent of developers); issue validation opinion.

web_checks.snippet: 1 month ago - It has to identify prompt injection, tool misuse, data exfiltration through legitimate outputs, and changes in the agent’s normal action graph. Re-approval triggers matter because agent behaviour can drift after approval through prompt changes, tool additions, or model updates. In identity terms, approval is a snapshot, while runtime control has to be continuous. Practical implication: tie detection coverage and drift-triggered re-approval into the release process so approval does not become a one-time paper exercise. Attacker objective: The attacker objective is to turn an approved AI agent into a governed-but-overreaching execution path that reaches data or systems beyond the intended boundary.

control_testing.objective: Fairness — AIDA decisions do not systematically disadvantage individuals/groups

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: For AI-assisted decisions that may materially affect people, fairness is assessed using appropriate methods and results are acted upon before deployment and after material change or drift.

design: 1) Inspect the fairness assessment standard and FEAT-aligned methodology. 2) Confirm it defines affected groups, relevant fairness dimensions/metrics, thresholds, dataset/population requirements, mitigation and independent validation for high-materiality use cases. 3) Confirm event-driven reassessment triggers for drift/material change are defined. PASS when the design can detect and manage systematic disadvantage for the intended decision context; FAIL when material groups/metrics/thresholds or mitigation are omitted; NOT TESTABLE when no approved fairness method exists.
operating: 1) For the sampled AIDA/use-case population, inspect the latest fairness results against approved thresholds and relevant groups. 2) Verify breaches/near-breaches triggered mitigation, escalation or restricted use and that re-testing occurred after material change/drift. 3) Trace any complaints or observed disparities to investigation and remediation. PASS when fairness performance is measured, thresholded and acted upon in operation; FAIL when systematic disadvantage is evidenced without effective response; NOT TESTABLE when the relevant population or metrics cannot be verified.

play_steps.action: Identify affected individuals/groups and analyse impact (fairness). Trigger the FEAT assessment per the FEAT Assessment Methodology (Veritas): Ethics & Accountability (F2/F3) set at org level, Fairness (F1) and Transparency (F4) run concurrently for the use case. For high-materiality use cases, initiate independent validation.
Complete privacy impact assessment (DPIA) where personal data is involved.
Document foreseeable misuse, predictable failure modes and proposed mitigations.
Assess societal/environmental impact for material or public-facing systems.
Review and sign off the impact assessment; record residual risk.

control_testing.requirement_basis: AI incidents have an AI-specific classification, escalation and recovery process with accountable responders, records and applicable external notification paths.

design: 1) Inspect the AI incident playbook, severity taxonomy, escalation matrix and regulatory-notification procedure. 2) Confirm roles, containment, evidence preservation, root-cause analysis, customer/stakeholder communications, lessons learned and notification decision criteria are defined, including reference to the currently applicable MAS notice/licence obligations. 3) Confirm required response/reporting timelines are explicit where applicable. PASS when the incident design is complete, attributable and time-bound; FAIL when material response or notification decisions are undefined; NOT TESTABLE when no controlled incident process exists.
operating: 1) Select a sample of AI incidents/near misses and trace detection, logging, severity classification, escalation, containment, notification decision, RCA and remediation. 2) Verify timestamps against applicable internal and regulatory timelines and confirm reasons for any non-notification decision. 3) Inspect whether lessons learned updated controls/tests where appropriate. PASS when incidents were handled, escalated and closed under the playbook and applicable regulatory obligations; FAIL when material response/notification steps were missed; NOT TESTABLE when incident records are absent or incomplete.

play_steps.action: Detect and log the incident; record time, system, symptoms, initial impact.
Triage severity and classify; convene responders.
Contain: disengage / rollback / activate kill-switch; isolate affected components.

Assess against the FSM-N05 (TRM) “relevant incident” threshold — severe/widespread operational impact, or material customer-service impact. If met: notify MAS within 1 HOUR of discovery (BCM hotline) and submit root-cause & impact report within 14 DAYS. Notify internal stakeholders in parallel.
play_steps.evidence: MAS notification (≤1 hr); RCA & impact report (≤14 days); stakeholder notification log

play_steps.action: Root-cause analysis; remediate; verify fix.
Post-incident review; update controls, tests and playbook.

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: AI and model changes are controlled through documented impact assessment, testing, approval and traceability from change request through implementation and post-implementation verification.

design: 1) Inspect the AI change-management policy and change taxonomy. 2) Confirm changes are categorised by materiality and require impact assessment, testing/validation, approval, implementation recording, rollback/emergency handling and post-implementation verification as applicable. 3) Confirm separation of requester/approver, version traceability and retrospective approval rules for emergency changes. PASS when the design covers the full change lifecycle and prevents uncontrolled deployment; FAIL when material changes can bypass assessment/approval/testing; NOT TESTABLE when no controlled change process exists.
operating: 1) Use the authoritative change-register population for the review period. 2) Check population integrity (unique IDs, completeness, required fields) and sample changes across materiality tiers. 3) For each sample, verify approval occurred before implementation, tested/versioned artefact matches deployment, emergency changes followed the exception path, and post-implementation verification was recorded. PASS when sampled and population-level checks support effective change control; FAIL when duplicate/stale/incomplete records or approval-after-deployment undermine control effectiveness; NOT TESTABLE when the source population is unavailable/incomplete.

play_steps.action: Re-run materiality assessment; confirm risk tier still correct.
Re-validate model; review monitoring history and drift since last review; re-run the FEAT assessment (fairness drift F1, transparency F4) per cadence — annual for high-materiality, plus event-driven.
Refresh impact assessment for any context/regulatory changes.
Decide: re-approve, require changes, or retire.

episodic.query: AI and model changes are controlled through documented impact assessment, testing, approval and traceability from change request through implementation and post-implementation verification.

control_testing.objective: Change management

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: AI and model changes are controlled through documented impact assessment, testing, approval and traceability from change request through implementation and post-implementation verification.

design: 1) Inspect the AI change-management policy and change taxonomy. 2) Confirm changes are categorised by materiality and require impact assessment, testing/validation, approval, implementation recording, rollback/emergency handling and post-implementation verification as applicable. 3) Confirm separation of requester/approver, version traceability and retrospective approval rules for emergency changes. PASS when the design covers the full change lifecycle and prevents uncontrolled deployment; FAIL when material changes can bypass assessment/approval/testing; NOT TESTABLE when no controlled change process exists.
operating: 1) Use the authoritative change-register population for the review period. 2) Check population integrity (unique IDs, completeness, required fields) and sample changes across materiality tiers. 3) For each sample, verify approval occurred before implementation, tested/versioned artefact matches deployment, emergency changes followed the exception path, and post-implementation verification was recorded. PASS when sampled and population-level checks support effective change control; FAIL when duplicate/stale/incomplete records or approval-after-deployment undermine control effectiveness; NOT TESTABLE when the source population is unavailable/incomplete.

play_steps.action: Re-run materiality assessment; confirm risk tier still correct.
Re-validate model; review monitoring history and drift since last review; re-run the FEAT assessment (fairness drift F1, transparency F4) per cadence — annual for high-materiality, plus event-driven.
Refresh impact assessment for any context/regulatory changes.
Decide: re-approve, require changes, or retire.

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: AI systems are evaluated and independently validated against defined criteria before deployment, with results, limitations, residual risk and re-validation triggers documented.

design: 1) Inspect the evaluation/testing standard, acceptance criteria and independent-validation procedure. 2) Confirm testing covers relevant performance, robustness, fairness, security, explainability and failure-mode dimensions, with risk-based thresholds and evidence-retention requirements. 3) Confirm independent validation is required where materiality warrants it and that unresolved defects block or condition release. PASS when the evaluation and validation design is risk-based, measurable and independent where required; FAIL when material tests/thresholds or independence are absent; NOT TESTABLE when no controlled test methodology exists.
operating: 1) Select a risk-based sample of validation packages, including at least one high-materiality system where available. 2) Reconcile test scope to approved requirements, review results against thresholds, inspect defects/exceptions and confirm independent validation sign-off. 3) Verify failed/conditional tests resulted in remediation, restricted release or documented approval under policy. PASS when tests were executed as designed and release decisions reflect results; FAIL when material tests were skipped, thresholds ignored or independence bypassed; NOT TESTABLE when validation evidence is incomplete.

play_steps.action: Sign off data quality, representativeness, lineage and provenance for training/test data.
Document model & feature selection, design decisions and requirements traceability.
Run testing & evaluation: performance, robustness, fairness/bias, security, explainability.
Independently validate the model (independent of developers); issue validation opinion.

control_testing.objective: Decommissioning / safe phase-out

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: AI systems can be safely decommissioned or phased out with controlled retirement, dependency closure, data/record retention and communication obligations.

design: 1) Inspect the decommissioning/safe-phase-out procedure. 2) Confirm criteria cover dependency/impact analysis, access/credential removal, data retention/disposal, customer/stakeholder communication where needed, documentation/log archiving and inventory closure. 3) Confirm required approvals and evidence retention are defined. PASS when safe phase-out steps and responsibilities are explicit; FAIL when material dependencies, data or access risks are not addressed; NOT TESTABLE when no controlled decommissioning procedure exists.
operating: 1) Sample retired/replaced AI systems from the inventory and trace the decommissioning record. 2) Verify dependent services/users were addressed, access/credentials removed, data disposition followed policy, logs/documentation archived and inventory status updated. 3) Check for residual production endpoints or stale entries. PASS when sampled systems were fully and safely decommissioned; FAIL when access, data, dependencies or inventory were left unresolved; NOT TESTABLE when the retirement population cannot be reconciled.

play_steps.action: Assess impact on dependent systems/users; plan safe phase-out.
Handle data retention/disposal per policy and privacy obligations.
Remove access and credentials; decommission infrastructure.
Archive documentation & event logs; update the AI inventory.

control_testing.objective: Accountability — clear internal & external accountability for AIDA-driven decisions

provenance.testing_fields: P: Test of Design; Q: Test of Operating Effectiveness

control_testing.requirement_basis: Accountability for AI-assisted decisions is explicit across internal owners, decision authorities and material third-party dependencies, with non-delegable internal accountability.

design: 1) Inspect the accountability matrix, internal authorisation records and third-party responsibility model. 2) Confirm accountable roles cover business owner, model owner, risk/control functions, decision authority, escalation and external/vendor responsibilities, with non-delegable accountability clearly defined. 3) Confirm approval and record-retention requirements. PASS when accountability is explicit from AI system through decision outcome, including material third-party dependencies; FAIL when responsibility is ambiguous or delegated without retained accountability; NOT TESTABLE when approved accountability artefacts are unavailable.
operating: 1) Sample material AI decisions, releases and third-party model arrangements. 2) Trace each to named accountable owners, required approvals, escalation paths and decision/authorisation records. 3) Inspect incidents/complaints to confirm responsibility was clear and exercised. PASS when sampled decisions have identifiable accountable owners and documented authorisation; FAIL when responsibility cannot be established or vendors are treated as replacing internal accountability; NOT TESTABLE when required decision records are unavailable.

play_steps.action: Identify affected individuals/groups and analyse impact (fairness). Trigger the FEAT assessment per the FEAT Assessment Methodology (Veritas): Ethics & Accountability (F2/F3) set at org level, Fairness (F1) and Transparency (F4) run concurrently for the use case. For high-materiality use cases, initiate independent validation.
Complete privacy impact assessment (DPIA) where personal data is involved.
Document foreseeable misuse, predictable failure modes and proposed mitigations.
Assess societal/environmental impact for material or public-facing systems.
Review and sign off the impact assessment; record residual risk.

proposal.sufficiency_basis: ASSESSMENT INCONSISTENCY: the model proposed PARTIAL, but every applicable canonical element is MET and no canonical gap survives validation. The validator is deliberately downgrade-only and will not manufacture an upgrade to FULL. The reviewer should verify expected artefact/operational-evidence coverage and either retain PARTIAL with a concrete gap or revise the sufficiency to FULL.
supplemental_assessor_notes: The same governance conditions hold for every proposed agentic action regardless of the system it originates from or the integration pattern used
